purpose: Discover a new metadata-only pool of recent merged ML systems fixes for prospective Development-task qualification after the prior 24-entry queue was exhausted.
hypothesis: A complete metadata-only scan of recent merged PRs in the six previously screened ML systems repositories will yield a tractable set of post-cutoff, small-diff fixes with changed test paths that can be manually checked for distinct task families and then deeply qualified.
cheaper_alternative_considered: The frozen 24-entry manual queue was already reconciled against Stage 2/3 exposure and contains zero fresh Development candidates. No model call or source checkout is needed for this metadata discovery pass.
primary_output: Count and immutable metadata of PRs that pass the frozen coarse screen; this is only a discovery output and cannot be used as task qualification or model-capability evidence.

discovery.api: GitHub GraphQL Search and PullRequest metadata fields

additional_prior_identities.reason: Previously exposed Development task outside the 24-entry manual queue.

coarse_screen.meaning: Manual-review shortlist only. Does not establish executable regression, grader independence, family distinctness, license suitability, model familiarity, or split eligibility.

stop_rules: Preserve partial metadata and record failure if GitHub search is incomplete, exceeds the 1,000-result ceiling, or any candidate metadata query fails.
Do not inspect PR source diffs, test contents, discussions, or task patches in this pass.
Do not open or execute any historical Held-out task or test.

Keep every source-level shortlist item UNQUALIFIED and UNASSIGNED until a separate prospective protocol pins source/test hashes, exposure checks, license review, baseline-fails/fixed-pass reproduction, and an independent grader.
limitations: A merge date after the 2025-08-09 public model training-completion proxy does not prove absence from pretraining.
GitHub titles and changed paths are not evidence that a task is independent, CPU-runnable, objectively gradable, or suitable for model evaluation.
A successful metadata scan is not a coding-agent attempt, policy update, Development success, or held-out result.
